title: Coordinate character extension and its Koszul derived boundary
statement:
Let $R$ be any commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Use internal $R$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and their ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $r\geq0$ and let $D=\mathbf Z^r$ be discrete, with trivial action on $R$ [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. For $i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}$, let $d_i:\underline D\to(R,+)$ be the condensed additive map induced by $(n_1,\ldots,n_r)\mapsto n_i1_R$, and let $\delta_i:R[-1]\to R\Gamma_{R,D}(R[0])$ be its connecting character class normalized as in [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. Put $K=K_R(R;1)$ with the subset signs of [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution], and let $u_I:R[-|I|]\to K$ denote the chain inclusion of the subset $I$ with coefficient $1$. Let $\lambda$ be any simultaneous triangulated, invariant-normalized comparison of [lem-sfb-lattice-koszul-triangulated-cup-comparison].

The formulas $E_i=R\oplus R$ and $T_j(x,y)=(x+\mathbf1_{j=i}y,y)$ define commuting invertible internal $R$-linear operators and an exact sequence of $D$-equivariant modules
$$0\longrightarrow R\xrightarrow{x\mapsto(x,0)}E_i\xrightarrow{(x,y)\mapsto y}R\longrightarrow0.$$
Its Koszul sequence is degreewise split by $s(y)=(0,y)$ and $\pi(x,y)=x$ on every subset component, as underlying internal modules. Let $\partial_i:QK\to(QK)[1]$ be its canonical derived connecting morphism, with $Q$ localization at quasi-isomorphisms. It is represented by the cochain map with components $\pi^{n+1}d_{K(E_i)}^n s^n$; its degree-zero component on the empty-subset inclusion has singleton $\{j\}$ component $\mathbf1_{j=i}1_R$. With the canonical shift comparison, the shifted composite $\partial_i\circ Q(u_\varnothing)$ is exactly $Q(u_{\{i\}}):R[-1]\to QK$. Consequently
$$\delta_i=\lambda_R\circ Q(u_{\{i\}})$$
as actual morphisms in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_R)$, with the positive character normalization. The zero ring is allowed; no characteristic, flatness, or completeness assumption is made.

proof.text: For a section $n$ of $\underline D$, set $n(x,y)=(x+d_i(n)y,y)$. Additivity of $d_i$ gives $n(m(x,y))=(x+(d_i(n)+d_i(m))y,y)=(n+m)(x,y)$; the inverse is $(x,y)\mapsto(x-d_i(n)y,y)$. These formulas are $R$-linear and natural under every profinite base change, as required by [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. On constant basis vectors they give exactly the displayed $T_j$, hence the operators commute. Both $a(x)=(x,0)$ and $p(x,y)=y$ are equivariant for trivial endpoints. Underlying modules have $\ker p=\operatorname{im}a$, $p$ is split surjective, and $a$ is split injective. By [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus], forgetting is exact and detects exactness, so this is a short exact sequence in the equivariant abelian category.

source.place: Paragraph (3), algebraic dense-lattice normalization: agent expansion of the coordinate-character boundary calculation.

proof.text: Apply the explicit finite Koszul construction of [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution] to the sequence. Equivariance makes $K(a)$ and $K(p)$ chain maps, since they commute with every $T_j-1$. In degree $n$, take the finite direct sum of $s(y)=(0,y)$ and $\pi(x,y)=x$ over all $n$-element subsets. On each component, $\pi a=1$, $ps=1$, and $a\pi+sp=1$. Thus the Koszul sequence is degreewise split exact as underlying internal modules, including degrees outside $0,\ldots,r$, where all objects are zero. The endpoint complexes are $K=K_R(R;1)$ and have zero differential because every endpoint operator is $1$. The sections $s$ and retractions $\pi$ here are only graded maps; no equivariance or compatibility with the middle differential is asserted.

source.place: Paragraph (3), algebraic dense-lattice normalization: agent expansion of the coordinate-character boundary calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus] with the trivial group to see that the internal module category is abelian. Apply [lem-sc-p1-split-ses-boundary-comparison] to the integer cochain complexes of step 2 and their displayed splittings. It gives the chain map $\beta:K\to K[1]$ with $\beta^n=\pi^{n+1}d_{K(E_i)}^n s^n$ and identifies its localization with the canonical short-exact-sequence boundary: $\partial_i=Q(\beta)$ with the canonical shift comparison. This is an equality with the canonical cone boundary, not merely the assertion that some triangle with these first two arrows is distinguished. The cited comparison uses the same positive split-boundary convention, with cone third arrow minus the projection.

source.place: Tags 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), 014I (definition-split-ses), 014Q (definition-distinguished-triangle); split cochain formula in homology.tex, Tag 011J (lemma-ses-termwise-split-cochain).

proof.text: Use the differential formula of [lem-sfb-discrete-lattice-koszul-resolution]. For a tuple $y\in K^n$ and a subset $J$ of size $n+1$, one has $(T_j-1)s(y_{J\setminus\{j\}})=(\mathbf1_{j=i}y_{J\setminus\{j\}},0)$. Consequently $(\beta^ny)_J$ is zero if $i\notin J$ and otherwise equals $(-1)^{\#\{j\in J:j<i\}}y_{J\setminus\{i\}}$. At $n=0$, the component for $J=\{j\}$ is $\mathbf1_{j=i}y$, with positive sign. Therefore $\beta u_\varnothing:R[0]\to K[1]$ is the map which is $1_R$ in the sole singleton $\{i\}$ and zero in the others. Shifting this chain map down by one identifies it with $u_{\{i\}}:R[-1]\to K$; all relevant source and target differentials are zero. Localizing gives $(\partial_i Q(u_\varnothing))[-1]=Q(u_{\{i\}})$ with the canonical shift identifications.

proof.text: Let $F=R\Gamma_{R,D}$ and $e:R[0]\to F(R[0])$ be its invariant unit. Regard the equivariant sequence as complexes in degree zero, and write $\partial_{E_i}:R[0]\to R[0][1]$ for its boundary. These objects are bounded below. Put $b_i:F(R[0])\to F(R[0])[1]$ equal to $F(\partial_{E_i})$ followed by the canonical shift comparison. The boundary and invariant-inclusion clauses of [lem-sfb-lattice-koszul-triangulated-cup-comparison] give $\lambda_R[1]\partial_i=b_i\lambda_R$ and $\lambda_RQ(u_\varnothing)=e$. Composing gives $\lambda_R[1]\partial_iQ(u_\varnothing)=b_ie$. By the connecting-class definition of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus], $(b_ie)[-1]=\delta_i$: the action of a section $n$ on $s(1)$ has defect $(d_i(n),0)$, so its normalized cocycle is $+d_i$. Shift this equality down and substitute step 4 to obtain $\delta_i=\lambda_RQ(u_{\{i\}})$. The comparison's flat-algebra cup clause is not used; the argument applies to every simultaneous triangulated, invariant-normalized comparison in the statement.

proof.text: For $r=0$ there is no coordinate $i$, so all coordinate assertions are vacuous. For $r=1$ the middle Koszul complex is $E_i\xrightarrow{(x,y)\mapsto(y,0)}E_i$, and the computed boundary is $+1_R$. For $R=0$ every module and every displayed map is zero and all equalities hold. The formulas use only finite sums, integer signs and the unit of $R$; in characteristic two the same formulas remain valid. No flatness or completeness condition has entered the argument.
